newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher except for gold.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher except for gold.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended higher Friday, except for gold which fell to new three year lows on more talk of central bank sales, rumored hedge fund activity, and some nervous producer hedging, traders said.

"The optimism of a year ago has been replaced by pessimism, in a market dominated by fund short selling, intermittent producer panic and central bank liquidation," CRU International analyst Tony Warwick-Ching said in a report issued Friday.
COMEX April gold ended down $1.10 an ounce at $343.40, after posting a new contract low at $339.40 intraday.

In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $341.50/00, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $339.75, the lowest fix since April 22, 1993. Spot gold closed in New York Thursday quoted $342.80/30.

The decline in gold Friday was led by selling in the bullion market in Asia and Europe, rather than by fund activity on COMEX though, after some traders reported heavy hedge fund activity in the OTC and bullion market recently.
The one month implied lease rate for gold in the bullion market was steady around 1.84 percent early Friday.

But short term implied gold lease rates rose earlier to around two percent late last week, suggesting some speculative shorting in the OTC and bullion market may have occurred by hedge funds seeking to take advantage of the seasonal drop in demand during the Muslim holiday month of Ramadan and the Chinese New Year holiday this week.
Ramadan ends next week and the Hong Kong tael market, which has been closed for the Chinese New Year holiday, reopens next Tuesday.

"Dealers continue to speculate about possible central bank gold sales, while potential investors are discouraged from buying by a combination of the central bank rumors, interesting markets elsewhere, and the simple fact that gold prices are falling, and who wants to buy into a declining market," CPM Group analyst Ted Kempf said.
But lower gold prices in the recent months has led to rising physical offtake in the Far East, apart from Japan, analysts noted.
Kilo-bar premiums rose to around $2.00 an ounce in Hong Kong before the Chinese New Year holiday, while European refiners are reporting their best business in three years.
Demand in Japan has been dampened though by the strength of the US dollar which saw 48 month highs against yen Friday.
Lower gold prices have unnerved producers though resulting in further light hedging by mid-ranking Australian gold miners this week, bullion dealers said.
The price of gold in Australian dollars fell to new five year lows Friday, while the gold price in South African rand fell to 11 month lows.
Gold remained the weakest contract in the complex Friday, with the spot gold/silver ratio falling to a 16 month low around 69.11 Friday.
COMEX March silver ended up 8.5 cents at $4.942 an ounce, after again finding support around $4.800, within the uptrend since early January.

Silver found support in the past month partly on talk of a US investment fund buying about 40 million ounces which helped to push up silver options volatilities, causing some options grantors to short cover and delta hedge, analysts said.
In the platinum metals group, NYMEX April platinum ended up $1.30 an ounce at $355.90, with the April NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread widening sharply to a four month high at $12.00 an ounce.
NYMEX March palladium gained a further $2.60 an ounce to $135.35, after palladium fixed in London at $130.50 Friday, its highest since August 2, 1996.
"Prices (of palladium) continue to be pushed higher by dealer and speculative buying based on concern about Russian exports and annual sales contracts," CPM Group's Kempf said.
Palladium futures hit all time highs on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) overnight, after jumping the daily limit of 22 yen per gram.
Japanese palladium traders said they had given up hope of receiving any Russian shipments before April.
Russian budget and administrative problems resulted in the postponement of the annual Russian-Japanese palladium supply contract in December.
((-Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1641; -email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com))
